reason: E1 shows Cr addition induces a triphasic microstructure and improves room-temperature strength and ductility in HfMoTaTiZrCrx, but it provides no high-temperature data and concerns a different base alloy system (HfMoTaTiZr vs. TiVNbTa). The extrapolation to high-temperature performance and to the TiVNbTa system is unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Cr addition to a refractory HEA can induce a multiphase microstructure (e.g., BCC1, BCC2, Laves phases)
Such a multiphase microstructure can simultaneously enhance strength and ductility at room temperature
The strengthening mechanism involves Laves phase-induced dislocation obstruction and stress redistribution by BCC phases
These effects observed in HfMoTaTiZrCrx will transfer to the TiVNbTa system with similar Cr additions
The room-temperature ductility enhancement or retention will persist at high temperature (1273 K)
